introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (0580 Physics 1, June 2023, Ordinary Level). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; select only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. No physical constants are printed on the paper: the answer key uses $g = 10\ \mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$ where needed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D. Section 1 (questions 1-42) has independent questions; Section 2 (questions 43-50) has two groups of questions about a practical situation (Questions 43-46 and 47-50).

figures.legende: Four graphs of g (vertical axis) against t (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A rises steeply then stays constant, B is a horizontal line, C is a rising straight line, D is a falling straight line (Question 4).
Section of ticker tape with seven dots between end Y (left) and end X (right), the spacing growing from Y to X, and an arrow labelled Direction of motion pointing towards X (Question 5).
Four graphs of V (vertical axis) against I (horizontal axis), labelled A to D: A straight line through the origin, B curve bending upwards, C curve bending over, D horizontal line (Question 18).
Resistors 3 ohms and 6 ohms in parallel, in series with a 5 ohms resistor, between points A and B (Question 20).
Wheelbarrow with the wheel at the right-hand end, the tray in the middle and the handle at the left; four positions A, B, C, D marked on the handle, A being furthest from the wheel (Question 26).

Four graphs with vertical axis Y (labelled V on D) and horizontal axis X, labelled A to D: A horizontal line, B straight line through the origin, C curve bending upwards, D decreasing curve (Question 36).
Velocity-time graph: velocity rises uniformly from 0 to 15 m/s at t = 10 s, then stays at 15 m/s until t = 20 s (Question 42).
Hydraulic jack: U-shaped tube of oil with an effort piston on the left and a load piston on the right (Questions 43-46).
Lagged calorimeter with liquid, stirrer, thermometer and electric heater connected to a battery, a voltmeter and an ammeter, to measure the specific heat capacity of a liquid (Questions 47-50).

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is a pair of scalar quantities?
questions.corrige_markdown: A scalar has magnitude only; a vector has magnitude and direction. Force, momentum and velocity are vectors, so options A, B and D each contain a vector. Energy and pressure are both scalars (pressure acts equally in all directions at a point). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is not a contact force?
questions.corrige_markdown: Friction, tension and upthrust all act through direct contact between two bodies (surface on surface, rope on object, fluid on object). Weight is the pull of the Earth's gravitational field and acts without contact. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The gradient of velocity-time graph represents:
questions.corrige_markdown: Gradient $= \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}$, which is the definition of acceleration. The area under the graph (not the gradient) gives the distance covered. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The variation of acceleration due to gravity ($g$) with time ($t$) can best be represented by which of the graphs in figure 1?

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Near the Earth's surface $g$ is constant ($\approx 10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$) whatever the time. The graph of $g$ against $t$ is therefore a horizontal straight line, which is graph B. Graph A would mean $g$ rises from zero and then levels off, C that it grows steadily and D that it decreases to zero. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
A trolley with a ticker tape attached to it, is caused to run down a runway. A section of the tape produced by a ticker timer of known frequency is displayed in figure 2.

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

The object is:

*Options as printed:* A) moving with constant velocity B) accelerating C) decelerating D) moving with constant acceleration
questions.corrige_markdown:
Reading the tape: the gap between consecutive dots is smallest at end Y and largest at end X, and it grows steadily from Y to X. Each gap corresponds to the same time (one tick of the timer), so a larger gap means a larger velocity. The dots are not equally spaced, so the velocity is not constant (option A is wrong).

Whether the object speeds up or slows down depends on which end of the tape was marked first. The tape is pulled through the timer by the trolley, so the end attached to the trolley is marked first. The arrow shows the direction of motion towards X, so X is the leading end and its widely spaced dots are the earliest: the object starts fast and the gaps shrink towards Y, so it is **decelerating** (option C). If the dots are instead read from Y to X in the order in which they were made, the object is accelerating (option B). The figure does not say which end is attached to the trolley, so the key cannot be fixed with certainty from the paper and no letter is designated. Standard method to remember: the dots made first are at the leading end of the tape, the end attached to the trolley.

questions.enonce_markdown: The form of energy stored in a car battery is:
questions.corrige_markdown: A car battery (lead-acid cell) stores energy in its chemicals and releases it as electrical energy when the chemical reaction takes place. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A builder raises a bag of cement of mass 50 kg onto a platform which is 3 m high. The work done by the builder in joules is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Work done against gravity = weight $\times$ height $= mgh$. Taking $g = 10\ \mathrm{N\,kg^{-1}}$ (the value is not printed on the paper):

$W = 50 \times 10 \times 3 = 1500\ \mathrm{J}$.

A common slip is to forget $g$ and use $mh = 150$ (option D). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following energy sources are all renewable energy sources?
questions.corrige_markdown: A renewable source is replaced as fast as it is used. The Sun and wind are renewable. Oil and coal are fossil fuels (non-renewable), so options A, B and D each contain at least one non-renewable source. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: What are the constituents of the nucleus?
questions.corrige_markdown: The nucleus is made of protons (positive) and neutrons (neutral), together called nucleons. The electrons orbit outside the nucleus. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The half-life of a sample of a radioactive substance is the time taken for the:
questions.corrige_markdown: Half-life is the time taken for the activity (the number of decays per second) of a sample, or the number of undecayed nuclei, to fall to half its value. The mass and size of the sample do not halve, because the decay products stay in the sample. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: activity of the sample to reduce by half
density of the sample to reduce by half
mass of the sample to reduce by half
size of the sample to reduce by half

questions.enonce_markdown: An object is placed 20 cm from a diverging lens of focal length 10 cm. The image formed is;
questions.corrige_markdown: A diverging (concave) lens always forms an image that is virtual, erect and diminished, on the same side as the object, wherever the object is placed. Check with the lens formula using $f = -10$ cm and $u = 20$ cm: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{3}{20}$, so $v = -6.7$ cm (virtual), and the magnification $\left|\dfrac{v}{u}\right| = 0.33 < 1$ (diminished). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a vacuum, all electromagnetic waves have the same:
questions.corrige_markdown: All electromagnetic waves travel at the same speed in a vacuum, $c = 3.0\times10^{8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Their frequencies and wavelengths differ (they are linked by $c = f\lambda$) and their amplitudes depend on the source. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A pond 8 m deep appears to be only 6 m deep when viewed vertically from above. The refractive index of the water is:
questions.corrige_markdown: For viewing from directly above, $n = \dfrac{\text{real depth}}{\text{apparent depth}} = \dfrac{8}{6} = 1.33 \approx 1.3$. Options A (the product $8\times 6$) and B (the sum $8+6$) come from misusing the numbers, and a refractive index of water is not as large as 2. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is true about a p-type semiconductor?
questions.corrige_markdown: A p-type semiconductor is made by doping pure silicon or germanium with a trivalent impurity (such as boron). Each impurity atom leaves one missing electron, a hole, so the holes are the majority charge carriers and outnumber the conduction electrons. The crystal as a whole stays electrically neutral, so A is false. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: It has a net positive charge
It has more conduction electrons than holes
It has more holes than conduction electrons
It has an equal number of holes and conduction electrons

questions.enonce_markdown: The electrical resistance of a metallic conductor is inversely proportional to its:
questions.corrige_markdown: $R = \dfrac{\rho L}{A}$. The resistance is directly proportional to the length $L$ and to the resistivity $\rho$, and inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area $A$ (a thicker wire has a lower resistance). For a metal, resistance also increases (not decreases) with temperature. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Alternating current is preferred to direct current for transmission of electrical power because:
questions.corrige_markdown: A transformer can step an alternating voltage up for transmission (high voltage, so low current and little $I^2R$ loss in the cables) and step it down for use. A transformer does not work with direct current. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: it can easily be stepped up and stepped down
thinner conducting wires can be used
it can easily be changed to direct current

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following elements can be used to dope silicon to produce a p-type semiconductor?
questions.corrige_markdown: A p-type semiconductor needs a trivalent (group III) dopant. Boron has three outer electrons. Phosphorus (group V) gives an n-type semiconductor, germanium is itself a semiconductor with four outer electrons, and iron is a metal not used for doping. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 3 best shows how the potential difference (V) across a metal conductor varies with the current (I) flowing through it?

![fig-3](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A metal conductor at constant temperature obeys Ohm's law, $V = IR$ with $R$ constant, so the graph of $V$ against $I$ is a straight line through the origin with gradient $R$. This is graph A. Curved graphs B and C describe non-ohmic components, and the horizontal line D would mean $V$ does not depend on $I$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The kWh is the unit of:
questions.corrige_markdown: $1\ \mathrm{kWh} = 1000\ \mathrm{W}\times 3600\ \mathrm{s} = 3.6\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{J}$: it is a unit of energy (power multiplied by time). The kilowatt (kW) alone is the unit of power. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 4 shows a connection of three resistors of resistances $3\,\Omega$, $6\,\Omega$ and $5\,\Omega$.

![fig-4](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)

The resultant resistance across AB is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The $3\,\Omega$ and $6\,\Omega$ resistors are in parallel: $\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $R_p = 2\,\Omega$. This combination is in series with the $5\,\Omega$ resistor: $R = 2 + 5 = 7\,\Omega$. Adding all three ($14\,\Omega$, option D) forgets that two of them are in parallel. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT released by a decaying radioactive nucleus?
questions.corrige_markdown: A decaying unstable nucleus emits alpha particles, beta particles and gamma rays. X-rays are produced outside the nucleus, when fast electrons hit a metal target or when electrons in the inner shells of an atom change energy level. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A car of mass 600 kg moving with a constant velocity of $20\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ along a straight road is brought to rest in 40 s by applying the brakes. The average retarding force acting on the car during this time is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Deceleration: $a = \dfrac{v-u}{t} = \dfrac{0-20}{40} = -0.5\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

Retarding force: $F = ma = 600 \times 0.5 = 300\ \mathrm{N}$.

The other options do not follow from $F = ma$ with these data (for example $1200\ \mathrm{N}$ would need a deceleration of $2\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following statements is an advantage of using a pressure pot to cook food?
questions.corrige_markdown: A pressure cooker is sealed, so the pressure above the water rises. The boiling point of water increases with pressure, so the food cooks at a temperature above $100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$ and therefore cooks faster. Options A and C state the opposite, and no cooking method preserves all nutrients. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: It cooks at a lower temperature
It cooks at a higher temperature
It cooks at a lower pressure
It preserves all the food nutrients

questions.enonce_markdown: When matter moves in a bulk and transfers heat from one point to another, the process is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: In convection the heated fluid itself moves in bulk (hot fluid rises, cold fluid sinks) and carries thermal energy with it. In conduction energy passes from particle to particle with no bulk movement; in radiation no matter is needed at all. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The advantage of the double wheels of a heavy truck is to:
questions.corrige_markdown: The weight of a heavy truck is shared among more tyres, so the total area in contact with the road is larger. Since $P = \dfrac{F}{A}$, the pressure on the road for the same weight is smaller, which protects the road surface from damage. Double wheels do not reduce friction (C) with the road. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: increase the stability of the truck
reduce the pressure exerted on the ground
reduce the friction between the wheels and the road
facilitate braking when the brakes are applied

questions.enonce_markdown:
At which of the marked positions in figure 5 is the lowest effort applied to lift the wheel barrow?

![fig-5](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The wheelbarrow is a lever of the second class: the pivot (fulcrum) is the axle of the wheel at the right-hand end, the load is the weight in the tray, and the effort is applied at the handles. Moment of effort about the pivot = moment of load about the pivot, so effort $= \dfrac{\text{load}\times\text{distance of load}}{\text{distance of effort}}$. The effort is smallest where its distance from the pivot is largest, that is at position A, the point furthest from the wheel. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A tennis ball is thrown at a wall with a velocity of $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and rebounds with a velocity of $4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. What is the change in velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Velocity is a vector. Take the direction towards the wall as positive: initial velocity $= +6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, final velocity $= -4\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (rebound).

Change in velocity $= -4 - 6 = -10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, a magnitude of $10.0\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The trap is to subtract the speeds ($6-4 = 2$, option C). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The lower fixed point of a mercury-in-glass thermometer in kelvin scale is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The lower fixed point is the ice point, $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$. In kelvin, $T = \theta + 273 = 0 + 273 = 273\ \mathrm{K}$. 373 K is the upper fixed point (steam point, $100\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$), and 0 K is absolute zero. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Water is used as a cooling liquid because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Water has a high specific heat capacity ($4200\ \mathrm{J\,kg^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$), so it absorbs a large amount of heat for a small rise in temperature, which makes it an effective coolant. The melting point is irrelevant to cooling, and although water is cheap, that is not the physical reason. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: it has a melting point of $0\,^\circ\mathrm{C}$
it has a high specific heat capacity

questions.enonce_markdown: The heat supplied to a substance during change of state goes to increase:
questions.corrige_markdown: During melting or boiling the temperature stays constant, so the average kinetic energy of the molecules does not change. The heat (latent heat) is used to overcome the forces of attraction between the molecules, which increases their potential energy. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the kinetic energy of the substance
the potential energy of the substance

questions.enonce_markdown: A conductor is charged by bringing a charged object close to it but not touching it. This process can be described as:
questions.corrige_markdown: Charging a conductor by bringing a charged body near it, without touching, is charging by induction. Friction and rubbing are the same process (the two bodies are rubbed together), and transfer needs contact. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following electrical devices operates effectively using a soft magnetic material?
questions.corrige_markdown: A soft magnetic material (soft iron) is easily magnetised and loses its magnetism as soon as the current is switched off. This is needed in the electromagnet of an electric bell, whose armature must be attracted and released many times a second. A loudspeaker uses a permanent magnet, which needs a hard magnetic material. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Repulsion is the surest test to confirm a magnet using another magnet because;
questions.corrige_markdown: A magnet attracts both the unlike pole of another magnet and an unmagnetised piece of iron or steel, so attraction proves nothing. Repulsion happens only between two like poles, so it can only occur if both objects are magnets. Options A and C are false statements; D is true but is not the reason repulsion is the surest test. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: repulsion can only exist between unlike poles of magnets
repulsion can only exist between like poles of magnets
attraction can only occur between like poles of magnets
attraction can occur between unlike poles of magnets

questions.enonce_markdown: Which property of waves affects the loudness of sound?
questions.corrige_markdown: Loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave: a larger amplitude carries more energy and sounds louder. Frequency (pitch) determines how high or low the note sounds. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: When a vibrating object reaches resonance;
questions.corrige_markdown: Resonance occurs when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the object. Energy is then transferred most efficiently and the amplitude of vibration becomes a maximum. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Which of the graphs in figure 6 is correct for $\sin i$ (Y) plotted against $\sin r$ (X) for light moving from air into a rectangular glass block ?

![fig-6](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: Snell's law: $\dfrac{\sin i}{\sin r} = n$, a constant for a given pair of media. Hence $\sin i = n\sin r$, so a graph of $\sin i$ (Y) against $\sin r$ (X) is a straight line through the origin with gradient $n$ (about 1.5 for glass). This is graph B. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Two forces of magnitudes 3N and 4N are acting on a body. The maximum resultant force that can be obtained is:
questions.corrige_markdown: The resultant is largest when the two forces act in the same direction: $3 + 4 = 7\ \mathrm{N}$. (It is smallest, $1\ \mathrm{N}$, when they act in opposite directions, and $5\ \mathrm{N}$ when at right angles.) **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The phenomenon of a wave which leads to the production of echo is called:
questions.corrige_markdown: An echo is sound that has been reflected from a hard surface (a wall, a cliff) and returns to the listener. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A transformer which has a laminated soft iron core is more efficient because:
questions.corrige_markdown: Lamination (thin sheets insulated from each other) cuts the paths of the eddy currents induced in the core, so less heat is produced in the core and less energy is wasted. Soft iron is easily magnetised and demagnetised, which also reduces hysteresis loss, but the effect of lamination specifically is to reduce the heating of the core. Options C and D would reduce efficiency. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: less energy is wasted reversing the magnetic domains
less heat is produced in the core
more heat is produced in the core
fewer magnetic field lines link the primary and secondary coils

questions.enonce_markdown: The region round a magnet where an object experiences a force is known as:
questions.corrige_markdown: A magnetic field is the region around a magnet in which a magnetic material, or another magnet, experiences a force. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Heat from the sun reaches the earth through the process of:
questions.corrige_markdown: Space between the Sun and the Earth is almost a vacuum, so neither conduction nor convection (which need matter) can carry the heat. The energy arrives as infrared and other electromagnetic waves, that is by radiation. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 7 is the velocity-time graph of a moving body. The distance covered during the first 10 s is

![fig-7](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The distance is the area under the velocity-time graph. For the first 10 s the graph is a straight line from $0$ to $15\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, so the area is a triangle: $\dfrac{1}{2}\times 10\times 15 = 75\ \mathrm{m}$. (The $150\ \mathrm{m}$ of option B is the rectangle of the next 10 s, from 10 s to 20 s.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 43 - 46

Figure 8 shows a hydraulic jack system which may be used to lift a car.

![fig-8](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)

The hydraulic jack system is:
questions.corrige_markdown: In a hydraulic system the pressure in the liquid is the same everywhere. A small force on a small piston produces the pressure $P = \dfrac{F}{A}$, which acts on a large piston and gives a much larger force there. The system is therefore a force multiplier. It does not multiply energy (the work done is not increased) nor pressure (which is equal on both sides). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Why is oil preferred to water in the jack system?
questions.corrige_markdown: Oil is used as the working fluid because it does not evaporate or boil away easily when the system is hot, it lubricates the moving parts and it does not rust the metal parts as water does. Of the options, only B is a correct reason. Water is nearly incompressible, so C is false; transparency (A) is irrelevant. Option D is not a general property of oil. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: oil has less bubbles of air than water

questions.enonce_markdown: The principle on which the above system functions is based on:
questions.corrige_markdown: The jack works on Pascal's principle: pressure applied to an enclosed liquid is transmitted equally to every part of the liquid and to the walls of the container. It is the pressure, not the force, that is transmitted equally. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The mechanical advantage of the machine is defined as the ratio of:
questions.corrige_markdown: $\text{Mechanical advantage} = \dfrac{\text{load}}{\text{effort}}$. The ratio of distances in options A and B is the velocity ratio (or its inverse), and option D is the inverse of the mechanical advantage. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: distance moved by load to distance moved by effort
distance moved by effort to distance moved by load

questions.enonce_markdown:
Questions 47 - 50

The setup in figure 9 is an apparatus used to measure the specific heat capacity of a liquid

![fig-9](gce-ol-physics-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)

The calorimeter is lagged in order to:
questions.corrige_markdown: Lagging is a thermal insulator placed around the calorimeter. It reduces the heat lost to the surroundings, so that nearly all the electrical energy supplied by the heater goes into heating the liquid. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: prevent heat loss to the surroundings

questions.enonce_markdown: The thermometer is used to:
questions.corrige_markdown: To find the rise in temperature $\Delta\theta$ of the liquid, the thermometer must give the temperature before heating and after heating. Even distribution of heat is the job of the stirrer, not the thermometer. **Answer: B.**

choix.texte: measure temperature of liquid before heating
measure temperature of liquid before and after heating
ensure even distribution of heat in the liquid

questions.enonce_markdown: The specific heat capacity of the liquid can be calculated using the formula:
questions.corrige_markdown: The electrical energy supplied by the heater is $E = IVt$ and the heat gained by the liquid is $Q = mc\Delta\theta$. If no heat is lost, $mc\Delta\theta = IVt$, so $c = \dfrac{IVt}{m\Delta\theta}$. Options B and C subtract or add quantities that have different units, and D is the inverse. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The stirrer is used to ensure that:
questions.corrige_markdown: Stirring mixes the liquid so that the heat from the heater spreads evenly and the thermometer reads the temperature of the whole liquid. It does not make the liquid cool faster or evaporate evenly. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: the cold liquid from the bottom rises
